meta.defaultTitle: Notchi — a native notch overlay for Windows
meta.description: Download Notchi, a native notch overlay for Windows 10 and 11. Browse every published version with changelogs, file sizes and checksums.

footer.tagline: A native notch overlay for Windows, inspired by the macOS notch and Dynamic Island.

rss.title: Notchi releases
rss.description: Every published Notchi release, including changelogs and pre-releases.

hero.tagline: A native notch overlay for Windows, inspired by the macOS notch and Dynamic Island.
hero.nonWindows: Notchi only runs on Windows. You can still browse every release from this site.
hero.noStable: There is no stable release available yet.

previews.title: Compact when idle. Ready when you hover.
previews.description: The notch stays out of the way, then expands with media controls, system stats, notes and files.

features.title: Built for the desktop
features.description: A focused set of tools that stays close at hand without taking over your screen.

alwaysOnTop.title: Always-on-top overlay
alwaysOnTop.description: Keeps the notch visible above other windows without appearing in the taskbar.

modes.title: Compact and expanded
modes.description: Stays compact while idle and expands smoothly when the cursor moves over it.

media.title: Media controls
media.description: Track info, album art, progress, seeking and playback controls through Windows SMTC.

dashboard.title: System dashboard
dashboard.description: Clock, date, battery, CPU, RAM and disk usage at a glance.

notes.title: Quick notes
notes.description: A dedicated notes window with automatic saving.

files.title: File drop shelf
files.description: Drag files onto the notch to open, reveal, copy paths or clear them.

anchor.title: Screen anchoring
anchor.description: Snap to the top center, left center or right center of the screen.

position.title: Persistent position
position.description: Remembers the last anchor and restores it on the next launch.

settings.title: Useful settings
settings.description: Choose which system metrics are visible and start Notchi with Windows.

lightweight.title: Lightweight by design
lightweight.description: Native WPF with no Electron or webview, and low idle resource usage.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.description: Notchi runs on 64-bit Windows 10 and Windows 11.

storage.label: Storage
storage.recommended: 250 MB free space on an SSD

requirements.note: The installer is per-user and does not require administrator privileges.

install.title: Install in three steps

step1.title: Download the installer
step1.description: Get the latest stable version from this site or the GitHub releases page.

step2.title: Run the installer
step2.description: The per-user installer starts right away and does not need administrator rights.

step3.title: Launch Notchi
step3.description: The notch appears at the top of your screen. Hover over it to expand.

install.smartScreenTitle: Windows may show a SmartScreen warning
install.smartScreenBody: The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows may warn you the first time. Choose “More info” then “Run anyway” only if you downloaded the file from this site or GitHub.
install.note: Looking for a beta? Pre-releases are listed on the versions page.

archive.title: All versions
archive.description: Browse every published Notchi release, including older versions and pre-releases.
archive.emptyBody: Notchi has not published a release yet. Follow the repository on GitHub to be notified.

version.verifyHint: Run this command in PowerShell and compare the hash with the one above.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.description: Install, verify, update and uninstall Notchi on Windows 10 and Windows 11.
docs.installIntro: Download the latest stable installer, run it, and launch Notchi from the Start menu.
docs.verifyBody: Every release lists a SHA-256 checksum. Download the installer, run the command below in PowerShell, then compare both hashes.
docs.verifyNote: If the hashes do not match, delete the file and download it again from GitHub.
docs.smartScreenBody: Notchi is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may show a warning. This is expected for new, unsigned software. You can verify the SHA-256 checksum before running the installer.
docs.uninstallBody: Open Windows Settings, go to Apps → Installed apps, select Notchi and choose Uninstall. Your notes are kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Notchi unless you remove them manually.
docs.autostartBody: Open Notchi settings and enable Start with Windows. You can turn it off again at any time.
docs.storageBody: Notes are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Notchi. Notes from older versions are migrated automatically.
docs.bugsBody: Report issues on GitHub so they can be tracked and fixed. Include your Windows version and the Notchi version you are using.

windows.question: Which Windows versions are supported?
windows.answer: Notchi supports Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, and Windows 11, on x64.

smartscreen.question: Why does Windows warn me about the installer?
smartscreen.answer: The installer is not code-signed yet. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning; verify the SHA-256 checksum before choosing “More info” then “Run anyway”.

admin.question: Does Notchi need administrator rights?
admin.answer: No. Notchi installs per-user under %LOCALAPPDATA% and does not require administrator privileges.

rollback.question: Can I install an older version?
rollback.answer: Yes. Every published release stays available on the all versions page.

notes.question: Where are my notes stored?
notes.answer: Notes are stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Notchi and are migrated automatically from older versions.

uninstall.question: How do I uninstall Notchi?
uninstall.answer: Open Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps, select Notchi, then choose Uninstall.
